column3: Buying the man in the picture rather than the pomade; the van, the dog and the surf are the actual proposition.
Suspicious of polished grooming brands; a cluttered real barbershop is the credential the product is borrowing.
Judges a product on the moment he runs his hands through it; the gesture is the demo.
Recognises the label before the claim; the illustrated lid is the shorthand he already trusts.
Chooses by shade name and box design; a distinctive name is what she screenshots and searches later.
Follows the brand for collections rather than products; new arrivals is the entire message.
Buys the co-sign; a musician's name on the box makes the colour a statement of allegiance.
Making a highly visible change and needs to see it on real hair first; the full result is the reassurance.
Wants the exact shade someone else achieved; naming the look as a recipe is what converts admiration into an order.
Needs to see the dye behave on texture like hers before risking it; the curl pattern is the qualifying detail.
Buys tools as much as products; tiny rollers is the mechanical detail that earns the demo.
Trusts a product that entered the house through someone close; the girlfriend framing removes the advertising suspicion.
Has learned that ordinary elastics cost her hair; satin is a defensive purchase against her own habits.
Watching hair come away in her hands and looking for anything to stop it; the fear is acute rather than cosmetic.
Has met the ingredient on social first and is now looking for a branded version she can just buy.
Times purchases to the annual sale and treats it as provisioning; the joke about survival supplies is aimed at a habit she already has.
Encounters the product on a shelf rather than a feed; showing the peg hook tells her where to physically find it.
Buys where she already shops weekly; a basket of the product in a familiar store is the whole ad.
Shops in warehouse quantities and compares member pricing; twenty-seven servings is the unit she thinks in.
Wants enough choice to avoid boredom but not enough to require a decision; two flavours is the sweet spot.
Waiting for a brand to reach the warehouse before trusting it at scale; in-store availability plus a coupon is the trigger.

column2: The Fifty-Something Man With A Number
column3: Has had bloodwork and now thinks in figures; a specific before-and-after testosterone reading is the format he believes.

column2: The Man Reading His Body As Symptoms
column3: Has four separate complaints and is being handed a single cause; puffy face and man boobs are named with deliberate bluntness.
Moves only when quantity and deadline combine; buy two get one with a countdown is the entire mechanism.

column2: The Long-Term Acne Sufferer Drawing It Herself
column3: Seven years of cystic acne makes her sceptical of polish; a hand-drawn before and after reads as a diary rather than a campaign.
Already inside a subculture with strong opinions about feet; a founder confessing he built a better version of a cult product speaks that dialect.
Has a specific daily discomfort and has been told synthetic is the cause; organic cotton is positioned as the fix.
Looking at an odd-looking product and needing it shown plainly; the clean studio shot lets him judge the shape without commitment.
Reads restraint as confidence; a wordmark on a plain field asks him to assume quality rather than be told it.
Believes toes should be able to spread and is buying anatomy, not fashion.
Was actively against the product and changed her mind; the reversal is more persuasive than any first-time endorsement.
Standing and walking all day; a man in transit with a backpack is the exact use case being sold.
Trusts a running tally over a testimonial; day fifty-seven implies evidence gathered rather than an opinion held.
Cannot get warm in bed and is being sold a very small, very specific fix.
Waits for the two-free offer; the sold-out tape doubles as scarcity and as proof.
Wants a checklist that tells her whether her symptom qualifies; three signs is an invitation to self-select.

column2: The Man With Swamp Foot At Work
column3: Has an embarrassing daily problem he has never named; blaming cotton reframes it as an equipment failure rather than a personal one.
Has decided synthetic fabric is the problem across his whole wardrobe; the product is defined entirely by what it removes.
Buys once something has been validated by other people's attention; calling it the viral pair is the reassurance.
Now reads garment tags the way he reads food labels; showing the care label is the proof shot.
